The provided excerpts delineate a rigorous mathematical audit of a software specification against its implementation, revealing profound structural divergences. We can model the Specification (S) as a formal algebraic structure defining permissible states and transitions, while the Implementation (I) represents a perturbed realization of S. The first primitive, Type Space Divergence, arises from T1-D1 and T1-D2. Here, the cardinality of the `VerificationStatus` set in I is strictly less than S ($|V_I| < |V_S|$), creating a projection singularity where unverified entities cannot be properly mapped. Simultaneously, the addition of `agentic-executor` expands the `ModelRole` space beyond S, introducing an orthogonal dimension not accounted for in the original metric tensor. This dual violation—truncation and expansion—destabilizes the foundational type theory.

The second primitive, Catalog Coupling Violation, stems from T1-D5. Mathematically, the function $f: \mathcal{T} \times \mathcal{C} \rightarrow \mathcal{R}$ (where $\mathcal{T}$ is TaskProfile, $\mathcal{C}$ is Catalog, $\mathcal{R}$ is Recommendation) is specified to be dependent on both arguments. However, I implements $f'(t, c) = f_{global}(t)$, effectively setting the partial derivative with respect to the catalog to zero ($\partial f / \partial c = 0$). This breaks the local diffeomorphism required for adaptive routing, locking the system into a global attractor regardless of local environmental variations.

Finally, Policy Graph Mutation (T1-D6, T1-D7) alters the transition matrix of the underlying Markov Decision Process. The introduction of an unsanctioned branch for `kind === 'agentic'` modifies the adjacency matrix, creating edges that bypass the prescribed complexity-based hierarchy. Conversely, the failure to utilize long-context locals (T1-D7) represents a zero-probability assignment to valid transitions, effectively pruning the state space and reducing the system's tactical depth. These primitives collectively demonstrate how minor syntactic deviations in code manifest as severe topological defects in the system's operational geometry.
